output.answer: Alphabet's latest results are Q3 2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026), reported October 28, 2026: revenues of $127.58 billion, up 25% year over year, with operating income of $40.58 billion (up 30%, 31.8% operating margin) and net income available to common stockholders of $26.17 billion, or diluted EPS of $2.12 — down from $2.87 a year ago because of an $8.22 billion loss in other income/expense (mark-to-market on equity stakes). It was Alphabet's first top- and bottom-line miss against Wall Street in nearly four years: adjusted EPS of $2.67 vs $3.02 expected and revenue of $127.58B vs $128.22B expected (LSEG), and the stock slumped more than 10%. The standout was Google Cloud, whose revenue more than doubled to $30.71 billion (+103%), while free cash flow swung negative to -$9.07 billion on $51.36 billion of capex; Alphabet maintained full-year 2026 capex guidance of $195-$205 billion and said capex will 'increase significantly in 2027'.
caveats: The $2.67 EPS is Alphabet's adjusted (non-GAAP) figure from CNBC's comparison with LSEG analyst estimates; Alphabet's reported GAAP diluted EPS was $2.12. The $2.12 decline vs $2.87 a year ago reflects an $8.22B negative swing in other income/expense (equity-stake marks), not weaker operations.

CNBC's LSEG estimates (EPS $3.02, revenue $128.22B, FCF -$2.70B, capex $55.09B) are analyst consensus figures from a news source, not Alphabet's own release; the operating figures themselves are from Alphabet's official release.
The '>$300 billion capex in 2027' figure is CNBC's characterization; Alphabet's own statement was that capex is expected to increase significantly in 2027, with details to come on the Q4 call.
Share-price reaction (slump of more than 10%) was the immediate post-earnings move on October 28, 2026 and may have changed since.

passages.quote:
MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. - October 28, 2026 - Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG, GOOGL) today announced financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

- Consolidated Alphabet revenues increased 25% to $127.6 billion, reflecting strong performance across the business and our 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth.

- Google Cloud delivered record growth as revenues increased 103% to $30.7 billion, led by strong growth in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across enterprise AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions, as well as core GCP services. TPU systems sales were also a meaningful contributor to revenue growth.
- Consolidated Alphabet operating income increased 30% and operating margin was 31.8%.
- Net income available to common stockholders was $26.2 billion and EPS was $2.12. Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, said: "We had a strong quarter and are now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate. Our deep full stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with Alphabet revenues growing 25% year-over year. Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-overyear query growth rate is the highest it's been in the last five years. Google Cloud revenues grew 103%, powered by huge demand for our AI infrastructure and AI solutions. We're also seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers. Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon are now leading at the frontier. Overall, our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times what we processed a year ago. On top of that, the Gemini app has reached one billion users-making it the fastest-growing product in Google's history-and we surpassed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, including trials. We're excited by the range of big opportunities ahead of us."

*   **Earnings per share**: $2.67 adjusted vs. $3.02 expected
*   **Revenue:** $127.58 billion vs. $128.22 billion

Revenue grew 25% from a year ago, but the company posted its first top-and-bottom-line miss in nearly four years.

Net income fell to $26.17 billion, or $2.12 per share, down from $34.98 billion, or $2.87 per share, a year ago.

*   Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion during the third quarter.
*   Revenue and earnings fell short of Wall Street expectations.
*   Alphabet maintained its full-year capex forecast after lifting guidance to between $195 billion and $205 billion during Q2.

As questions mount over heightened spending on the AI buildout, Alphabet's capital expenditures totaled $51.36 billion in Q3, falling short of the $55.09 billion expected by analysts. Investors are looking for a substantial return on investment to warrant the big spending plans from the hyperscalers.

Alphabet maintained its full-year capital expenditures forecast after lifting guidance to between $195 billion and $205 billion during the second quarter from $190 billion. Annual capex is expected to top $200 billion before exceeding $300 billion in 2027.

"We continue to expect our capex to increase significantly in 2027, and will provide further details on our Q4 call," finance chief Anat Ashkenazi told analysts during an earnings call.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q3 2026) on October 28, 2026.
Consolidated Alphabet revenues were $127.577 billion, up 25% year over year (from $102.346 billion), the 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth.
Adjusted EPS was $2.67 vs $3.02 expected and revenue $127.58B vs $128.22B expected (LSEG consensus) — Alphabet's first top-and-bottom-line miss in nearly four years.
Net income available to common stockholders was $26.170 billion and GAAP diluted EPS was $2.12 (vs $34.979 billion and $2.87 in Q3 2025).
Other income (expense), net was -$8.221 billion vs +$12.759 billion a year earlier; CNBC attributed the loss to equity holdings including SpaceX and Anthropic stakes ($8.66B loss in the category).
Operating income rose 30% to $40.576 billion; operating margin was 31.8%.

Google Cloud revenues increased 103% to a record $30.709 billion (vs $15.157 billion a year ago), a record growth rate, beating the $28.7B analyst estimate; TPU systems sales were a meaningful contributor.
Google Services revenues rose 11% to $96.302 billion; Google Search & other grew 12% to $63.350 billion (below the $64.96B estimate); YouTube ads were $11.207 billion (vs $10.261B).
Q3 free cash flow was negative $9.065 billion (vs -$2.70B expected by analysts) on capital expenditures of $51.36 billion (vs $55.09B expected).

Alphabet maintained its full-year 2026 capex forecast of $195-$205 billion (lifted from $190 billion during Q2), and CFO Anat Ashkenazi said capex is expected to increase significantly in 2027 (CNBC: annual capex expected to top $200 billion before exceeding $300 billion in 2027).
Alphabet shares slumped more than 10% after the report, which also showed long-term debt climbing to $125.1 billion from $21.6 billion a year earlier (~479% increase).
CEO Sundar Pichai said Alphabet is on a half-trillion-dollar revenue run rate; the Gemini app reached 1 billion users and YouTube Music & Premium surpassed 150 million subscribers (including trials).

In October 2026 the Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.22 per share on Class A, B and C stock (payable December 14, 2026), plus a $15.63-per-share quarterly dividend on mandatory convertible preferred stock.
